issue.title: bob capture TEXT help claims unknown --flag before -- is rejected, but the guard only checks where TEXT begins

task_type_fields.impact: `bob capture --help` misleads users and frontends such as Bob Mac Capture about which flags are refused, so a mistyped option after the text is silently captured as task text even though the help suggests it would be caught.
task_type_fields.repro:
The capture TEXT argument's help (src/native/capture/cli.rs:657-659, `text_arg`) says "unknown `--flag` before `--` is rejected". The guard that enforces this (`capture_flag_guard::find_unknown_long_flag`, called from src/native/capture/mod.rs:149, documented at mod.rs:180 as rejecting "an unknown alphabetic long option found where TEXT would begin") only inspects the position where TEXT begins. Once TEXT has started, later `--flag`-shaped tokens stay literal task text. For example, `bob capture buy milk --foo` captures "buy milk --foo" instead of rejecting it, although the help implies it would be rejected.

Fix: make the generated help (and any generated docs reference built from it) say exactly what the guard does, for example "an unknown `--flag` where TEXT would begin is rejected; later tokens stay literal". Alternatively, decide deliberately to widen the guard, but that is a behavior change that needs its own decision. Read the docs memory before editing user-visible CLI help and run `just docs-check`.

Provenance: first reported, unfixed, in the body of bob-cli commit 1194779f (agent chop.refresh_docs.bob-cli.2). The batch-9 lander (bob-cli-an.6.6.6.5.6.5.5.6.land) confirmed the help text and guard scope in source while reviewing post-start drift. The guard came from 0afeb2f3 (bob-cli-an.6.6.6.2, closed), the fix for closed bob-cli-8a.

issue.creation_reason: The batch-9 lander found this unfixed source follow-up in post-start drift commit 1194779f and confirmed it in source; nothing tracked it, and the help misstates refusal behavior.
